I farm the way a 60-year-old man with 40 years in the field farms: I keep the plan steady, not fancy, and I match it to my land, labor, and water. I have only 10.1 mu and a 2-person household, so I will not spread myself too thin. Because my main system is wheat-maize and I have well irrigation, I will keep most of the land in that rotation. That is the most familiar and dependable part of my farm, and I know how to manage it well. I will keep a smaller piece in cotton because I already grow it, it fits my experience, and it gives me some crop diversity instead of putting everything into one pattern.

For seed, I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps yield and uniformity, because after 40 years I care more about stable output than saving a little on seed. For fertilizer, I will stay moderate rather than push too hard. Wheat and maize will get the stronger nutrient input because they are my main food and cash crops in the rotation, while cotton will get a middle level. Since I have well irrigation, I will use it to protect yield, but I will not overwater because that costs money and labor. I will also keep pesticide use controlled and practical, based on the crops’ usual pressure in my area. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage on most fields because it is efficient for my scale and fits how I would manage residues and seedbed preparation. My goal this year is stable production, manageable labor, and lower risk rather than chasing the highest possible yield.
